title: `round(DOUBLE, d)`: an overflowing result keeps the input
description: DuckDB rounds to `d` digits: `round(x · 10^d) / 10^d` for `d ≥ 0` and `round(x / 10^-d) · 10^-d` below zero, and gives `x` itself where that is not finite (`round(1.5e308, -308)` is `1.5e308`). Below zero, when `10^-d` is infinite, every finite `x` gives 0 (`round(1.5e308, -309)` is 0). DuckDB 1.4.1 gave 0 wherever a negative `d` left no finite result, which `duckdb-R15-round-digits` recorded.
reference: `FloatCode.roundTo` (`core/Sverify/Core/Float.lean`) follows DuckDB 2.0's formula, and the Polars and SQL writers write it.

provenance.notes: v2.0.0's `RoundOperatorPrecision` returns 0 when the modifier is infinite and the input when the rounded value is infinite or NaN; v1.4.1 returned 0 in both cases for a negative precision.

provenance.checked_by: claude/api-to-sql-spark (#800); tests/test_numeric.py::test_round_to_digits_is_duckdbs found it with xs=[1.5e+308], d=-308

evidence.sql: SELECT round(1.5e308::DOUBLE, -308), round(-1.5e308::DOUBLE, -308), round(1.5e308::DOUBLE, -309), round(5e307::DOUBLE, -308), round(42.0::DOUBLE, -1000)
